Once you have enough CR to enter a higher difficulty CR gets less important.
In PVP this effect is capped at 10%. In PVE the cap is 11.3%.

The value of the primary attributes (Strength, Fortitude, Willpower, Vitality) on Primary Gear is dependant on your paragon level and the difficulty your character has unlocked.
Primary Stats on your Primary Gear are important but also pay attention to the magic affixes as these are mostly % based modifiers that can be extremely powerful.
If you look at your primary attack for example a gear piece with 100 points of strength more than your current piece offers you +30 more damage.
If you have a total of 10000 (primary attack) damage and one of the magic affixes is a "primary attack +4.5% damage increase" that means +450 more damage.
These % based modifiers are not visible in the stats of your character but are applied during combat.

When you extract Gem Power your Gem becomes dormant. However you can still socket it. It will re-awaken with all its effects when the Resonance Gems
inside the Gem are filled with equal or more Gem Power than the now dormant Gem had before
The "new" Resonance of the Gem is:
Original Resonance of the Ranked Gem (e.g. 1000 for a R10 5/5)
Reduced Resonance of the Resonance Gems (e.g. 2 per Rank for a 2-Star and 10 per Rank for a 5-Star)
Additional Resonance ( = Gem Power of all socketed Resonance Gems / 125 (for "correct" gems) or 200). This only works with R10 5* Gems
When you reach 6000 Resonance you are able to slot up to 4 additional legendary gems into your wings
The next Wing Slots are available at 7000 Resonance, then 8000 Resonance and over 8500 Resonance the current maximum amount of 16 additional Slots is available
When reaching 10000 Resonance, a new ultimate skill is available for each class.
When reaching 12000 Resonance Swift Heaven Movement Speed Bonus in safe zones is active
The current maximum possible Resonance is 13024
Refinement is a % multiplier for damage / life that is incereased by the ranks of your normal gems.
For each Rank of a socketed gem 3% of the base damage or 3% of the base life of the equipment piece that the gem is socketed in are added to your overall life / damage
Because all Gem Slots count towards the bonus try to get Set Pieces with triple Gem Slots

column2: If you manage to land a Critical Hit, your Armor Penetration Stat is compared to your Opponent's Armor Stat (PVP). If your AP is higher, then you can deal up to
58% more Critical Hit Damage because of your Armor Penetration (in PVE this Stat is measured against a fixed value depending on the diffculty).
So it makes sense to stack Armor Penetration alongside Critical Hit Chance.
The second benefit besides added value on Critical Hits is the amount of damage you deal when your opponent blocks a hit.
Because when he/she blocks a hit, your Armor Penetration is compared to the enemy Armor and the higher your AP is over their Armor, the less damage they will block (from a base of 50%)
The below table shows all sources of Armor Penetration. If all were maxed out you could theoretically have over 11.000 AP. More realistically,
Your Critical Hit Chance without any bonus stats is 3% by default.

Your Armor Stat does not reduce all damage you take. Armor is only applied in 2 cases:
1. When blocking damage, the higher your Armor is compared to your opponents Armor Penetration, the more damage you will block from a base of 50%.
This means if you block, you will always block at least 50% of the damage + whatever extra amount of reduction your Armor Stat gives you.
In PVE it is compared to a fixed value that is required for each Difficulty.
2. When receiving a Critical Hit, the higher your Armor is compared to your opponents Armor Penetration, the more of the bonus critical hit damage is reduced
Critical Hits cannot  be blocked, so the 200% damage is never reduced, only the bonus part is reduced (if your Armor is higher).
So stacking Armor only makes sense if you are also stacking Block Chance, otherwise you are just mitigating a little bit of extra Critical Hit damage
Your Block Chance default value without additional bonus factors is 6%

In PVP, the amount of damage you take is strongly dependant on the comparison of your armor vs your opponents armor penetration
Everytime you block a hit, these two stats are compared and the damage you take (from a base of 50% because you blocked the hit) is either reduced or increased.
Furthermore if you get critically hit, these stats determine if you take the full critical hit bonus damage or if its "just" the critical hit.
Critical Hit Damage Increase(PVE) = 59,5% * [ ( Player AP - Monster Armor) / Player AP - Monster Armor + 77 ) ]
Block Damage Reduction(PVE) = 19,8% * [ ( Player Armor - Monster AP) / Player Armor - Monster AP + 78 ) ]

So the difference between having a high Armor stat vs a low Armor stat in comparison to your opponent is taking 40.000 dmg more (when blocking)
If you get critically hit, you take 74.500 more dmg when your Armor stat is weak
Let's say you have 500.000 Life and you block evey hit. That's a difference of being hit 7 times before you die and 17 times.
If you are the Attacker, your Potency Stat is compared to the Defenders Resistance Stat. If your Potency is higher, the duration of your harmful effects will be extended.
More information on harmful effects in general can be found on the Game Page
Potency increases DoT time, however for the bleed to occur 1 x time, the time interval of the increase of the duration needs to be >1 sec (30% higher Potency)
The Cap in PVP for increased Duration because of higher Potency is 50%, so a DoT that lasts 1s can only be extended to 1.5s, so a second "Tic" will never happen
For example a 3s duration DoT that has 3 Tics would need a 40% extended duration to add another Tic, so your Potency vs. Opponents Resistance

So it is more efficent to stack Resistance, especially if you are F2P.

column2: When an enemy inflicts a harmful effect on your character, your Resistance Stats is compared to his Potency Stat to deduct if the effect will last longer or be shortened.
In Battlegrounds, when the attackers potency is higher than the targets resistance the duration of harmful effects can be up to 50% longer
But when the targets resistance is higher than the attackers potency, the duration can be shortened by up to 35%.
The difference between super high and super low resistance is around 57% shorter cc effects, 0.65/1.5=0.43.
Or in other words if your resistance is super low you get CC'd for 2.3x longer than when it's super high.
In PVE your Resistance Stat is compared to a fixed value that depends on the Difficulty (see below).

column2: Let's assume you have 20.000 damage and your Critical Hit Damage % Stat GEAR is 15% and you manage to land a Critical Hit.
If your Armor Penetration is equal to the Opponent's Armor Stat, you would deal 20.000 x [200% + 0 + 15%] = 43.000 damage
If your Armor Penetration is much lower than the Opponent's Armor Stat, you would deal 20.000 x [200% + (100% - 70%)*15%] = 40.900 damage
If your Armor Penetration is much higher than the Opponent's Armor Stat, you would deal 20.000 x [200% + 57% + 15%] = 54.400 in PVE or
45.000 damage in PVP, because the bonus from Armor Penetration is capped at 10% for PVP

So stacking Armor only makes sense if you are also stacking Block Chance, otherwise you are just mitigating a little bit of extra Critical Hit damage
